scene: At the Deer Park near Bārāṇasī, the Buddha asks five monks about five categories of experience.
question: Is it reasonable to say of any of these five changing parts of experience, 'This is mine, I am this, this is my self'?
main_point: Each of the five can cause trouble, changes over time, and cannot be made to obey your wishes. So the text says none is fit to be treated as 'mine,' 'I am this,' or 'my self.' It connects seeing this clearly with release.
reading_cue: The same argument is repeated for all five categories. Use the first one to learn the pattern. Later, watch for the repeated line: 'This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.'
not_saying: This passage is not trying to prove that nobody exists. It focuses on whether these five changing parts of experience are fit to be treated as 'mine,' 'I am this,' or 'my self.'
